Energy Policy 
Version 1.0 
| P a g e 5 
1. 
Introduction
SETU is committed to the efficient use of all energy across all campuses and activities with the 
purposes of reducing carbon emissions, optimising energy efficiency, mitigating the effects of 
climate change and preserving natural resources. 
The Climate Action and Low Carbon Development (Amendment) Act 2021, requires all public 
bodies including SETU, to align with national climate goals which are currently 50% Energy 
Efficiency improvement, against a 2006 to 2008 baseline and an absolute carbon reduction of 
51% against an average of 2016 to 2018 baseline by 20301.
2. 
Purpose
The purpose of this Energy Policy is to support and integrate with our broader 
energy management system, ensuring alignment with the international energy 
management standard ISO 50001:2018. 
3. 
Scope
This Policy applies to all students, employees (whether employed on a permanent, fixed 
term or temporary contract), trainees, seconded staff, agency staff, consultants, or third 
parties acting on behalf of or engaged by the University. 
It is the responsibility of: 
•
all students, employees, and relevant parties as outlined above, involved in energy 
consumption to familiarise themselves with the content of this Policy and to adhere 
to the expected standards; and
•
all infrastructure Building design teams (in accordance with their Conditions of 
Engagement) will be required to comply with this Policy and to inform all relevant 
associated parties of the requirements to comply with this Policy.
The Policy shall be made generally available and published publicly via the University 
website. 
4. 
Principles
The guiding principles of this energy policy as part of ISO50001:2018 require that the 
policy: 
•
is appropriate to the purpose of the organisation;
•
provides a framework for setting and reviewing objectives and energy targets;

Energy Policy 
Version 1.0 
| P a g e 6 
•
includes a commitment to ensure the availability of information and necessary 
resources to achieve objectives and energy targets;
•
includes a commitment to satisfy applicable legal requirements and other 
requirements related to energy efficiency, energy use and energy consumption;
•
includes a commitment to continual improvement of energy performance and the 
overall SETU energy management system;
•
supports the procurement of energy efficient products and services that impact 
energy performance;
•
supports design activities that consider energy performance improvement.
5. 
Policy
SETU is committed to the efficient use of all energy across all campuses and activities with 
the purposes of reducing carbon emissions, optimising energy efficiency, mitigating the 
effects of climate change and preserving natural resources. Management will lead and 
promote energy efficiency and support others in their roles as they relate to energy and 
decarbonisation. 
Through this Energy Policy SETU will: 
•
Ensure all legal requirements relating to energy use, consumption and efficiency 
are met and where possible improved.
•
Provide information on energy and demonstrate through energy awareness 
programmes how staff, students and service providers can influence energy 
consumption and promote energy efficiency and a
•
shared responsibility for energy consumption at all levels of the organisation.
•
Promote investment in energy efficient products, services in building refurbishment 
and new construction, incorporating Near Zero Energy building design and 
support design activities that consider energy performance improvements.
•
Provides a commitment to ensure the availability of information and necessary 
resources to achieve the University objectives and energy targets;
•
Set energy objectives and targets and review these regularly as part of a continual 
improvement process.
6. 
Responsibility and Authority
Senior management shall ensure that the responsibilities and authorities for relevant roles 
are assigned and communicated within the organisation, as per clause 5.3 of ISO50001:2018 
standard. This information is also contained in the SETU Climate Action Roadmap. In 
addition, senior management shall assign the responsibility and authority to the energy 
management team for:

Energy Policy 
Version 1.0 
| P a g e 7 
•
ensuring that an energy management system is established, implemented, 
maintained and continually improved;
•
ensuring that the energy management system conforms to the international 
energy management standard ISO50001:2018.
•
implementing action plans to continually improve energy performance;
•
reporting on the performance of the energy management system and 
improvement of energy performance to senior management at determined 
intervals;
•
establishing criteria and methods needed to ensure that the operation and 
control of the energy management system are effective.
7.
Compliance
It is expected that all employees of the University will comply with this policy.

9.
Review of Policy
This policy will be reviewed in advance of the review date, every 3 years from approval date 
and/or as soon as possible following new or updated legislation, national or sectoral policy. 
10. Policy Author
The author of this policy is the Climate Action Manager. Any feedback or issues arising on 
implementation of this policy should be communicated to the policy authors. They are 
responsible to ensure that the Policy Owner is aware of these comments when reviewing the 
policy.
